clue.text: Lard once used in the kitchen

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over or knocked about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook's note that some old lard got used up in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' signals the anagram of LARDONCE. The definition is loose: a strainer is one of the things found in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer for draining vegetables or pasta is standard kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Conspicuous union leader about to make proposal

parts.note: conspicuous means overt, plainly seen

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from union

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A prominent trade union boss is about to put forward a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening offer in negotiations, as in making peace overtures, is a proposal.

clue.text: Victory song put on by the victor

explanation.surface: A celebratory anthem performed by the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: First a song (an air) celebrating victory; then the expression a winner wears or puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, so a tune of victory; and a winner's look of exultation is also described with this phrase.

clue.text: Idiot acquires counterfeit sovereign

parts.note: duff is slang for fake or worthless
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen or sovereign

explanation.surface: A fool ends up holding a forged gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old British gold coin, which is the surface reading; here it is the monarch, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An incompetent or foolish person is a duffer in British slang.

clue.text: In the Kalahari chameleons are abundant

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A nature note: the desert of southern Africa teems with chameleons.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich and abundant both describe plentiful supply, as in a rich harvest.

clue.text: Just habits familiar to golfers

parts.note: just means fair, equitable
habits are ways, customary practices

explanation.surface: Fair-minded customs that golfers know well.
explanation.definitionFit: The mown strips between tee and green on a golf course are well known to every player.

clue.text: Record nothing but a trademark

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A complaint that a firm has registered nothing except its trademark.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's emblem or symbol is a brand mark used in trade.

clue.text: Managing director to whom one is indebted

indicators.note: managing as in handling or arranging, so the letters of director are reorganised

explanation.surface: The company boss is the person one owes money to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managing director' reads as a job title, but 'Managing' is the anagram signal on DIRECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender is the party a borrower owes money to.

clue.text: Popular king enters love affair ready to fight

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: enters says one piece goes inside another, here the king inside the love affair

parts.note: an amour is a love affair
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A well-liked monarch begins a romance, prepared for combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight clad in protective steel plate is equipped for battle.

clue.text: One embraced by the woman's successor

indicators.note: embraced by says the first piece is held inside the next

parts.note: her is the possessive of she, the woman's
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A child is hugged by the mother who names him successor.
explanation.definitionFit: The person next in line to inherit a title or estate succeeds to it.

clue.text: Confidentially, the stylus is out of action

definitions.text: the stylus is out of action

explanation.surface: A secret tip that the record-player needle has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally, the needle has been lifted away from the disc; as an idiom, said in confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark made unofficially, not for publication, is confidential; and a raised gramophone needle is literally lifted from the disc.

clue.text: Oppose general direction taken by a singer

parts.note: to counter something is to oppose it
tenor means the general drift or course, as in the tenor of a speech

explanation.surface: A general sets off on a path, taking a singer against orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general direction' looks military, but tenor is the general drift of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A male vocalist singing in the alto range, above the usual tenor voice.

clue.text: Fawn and ram on higher ground

parts.note: a butter is one who butts, as a ram does
up means raised, on higher ground

explanation.surface: A young deer and a ram standing on the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' is a verb, to flatter, not the young deer; 'ram' is the thing that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter someone obsequiously is to fawn upon them.

clue.text: Steal and cook fish?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to steal a fish and cook it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take game unlawfully is theft; and gently simmering fish in liquid is a cooking method.

clue.text: A stubborn fellow takes time to display charm

parts.note: a mule is proverbially stubborn, so a mulish person

explanation.surface: An obstinate man takes his time before showing off a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman worn to ward off evil is a charm.

clue.text: About to find a fairy

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of meeting a fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: Peri- is a Greek prefix meaning around or about (perimeter); a peri is a fairy of Persian myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek prefix signifies around, as in perimeter; and in Persian legend a beautiful sprite is so called.

clue.text: Sententious character of old explorer retiring in America

parts.note: Marco Polo was the medieval Venetian traveller

indicators.note: retiring as in drawing back, so the word in is read backwards

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: An explorer from the past withdrawing to live in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns IN into NI. The pompous old courtier of Hamlet is famed for platitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's lord chamberlain is a byword for pompous moralising, giving advice like neither a borrower nor a lender be.

clue.text: Many a girl has style

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral hundred, so many
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Plenty of girls are stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance or quality, as in she has real class, means style.

clue.text: Price paid by woman for aromatic plant

parts.note: cost means price
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman pays for a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant herb of the daisy family once used to flavour ale.

clue.text: Some of them negotiate a reasonable rent

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A few tenants bargain for a fair rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not money paid for housing but a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a split or rip in cloth, from the verb rend.

clue.text: Forbear to make an escort distressed

indicators.note: distressed as in disturbed or upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Advice to refrain from upsetting a chaperone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbear' looks like the verb, to refrain; it is the noun, a forefather (also spelt forebear).
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom one is descended, a forefather.

clue.text: The acid test for literature and music

parts.note: mus is the abbreviation for music

explanation.surface: A trial of an arts student's knowledge of books and music.
explanation.walkthrough: This indicator paper turns red in acid, so the test for acidity in chemistry is done with it; it also means a decisive test.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicator paper is literally used to test acidity, and figuratively a decisive trial is called this kind of test.

clue.text: High Churchman wanting God's favour

parts.note: his, capitalised, refers to God, so God's
grace is divine favour

explanation.surface: A senior cleric seeking the Almighty's blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Archbishops and dukes are formally addressed by this honorific title.

clue.text: Loafer dressed in a petticoat

explanation.surface: A layabout wearing an underskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A loafer is a shoe without laces; a slip is a petticoat, so in one is wearing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A laceless shoe is pulled on easily; and wearing an underskirt is having a slip on.

clue.text: When seraphim assembled in state

indicators.note: assembled as in put together from parts, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: The angels gathered in some unnamed state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' signals the anagram of WHENSERAPHIM. The answer is a US state in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, in New England, is a state.

clue.text: Nick has to administer a beating

explanation.surface: A police arrest followed by a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to whip something is to steal it, as is to nick it; and to flog with a lash is to beat.

clue.text: Gamble on finding a small monocle

explanation.surface: Taking a chance on locating a little eyeglass.
explanation.walkthrough: On spec means as a speculation; one lens of a pair of specs, taken singly, is a little eyeglass.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculation is a gamble; and one lens of spectacles, a single eyeglass, makes a monocle.

clue.text: Typical measures by crazy people

explanation.surface: Measures characteristic of mad people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Typical' means typographical here: printers call an en space a nut. Crazy people are nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers called an en space a nut, to avoid confusion with em; and mad people are slangily nutcases.

clue.text: An Italian with one poem for all mankind

parts.note: un is the Italian for an
I is the Roman numeral one
a verse is a poem

explanation.surface: An Italian writes a poem dedicated to the whole of humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An Italian' means the word an in Italian, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole world and everyone in it, as in the entire human race.

clue.text: Rory can't possibly be perverse

indicators.note: possibly as in one possible arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Rory couldn't conceivably be awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deliberately awkward and opposed is the same as being perverse.
